turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. 

Um, I hope I'm in the right place, and I don't want to make a huge deal out of it, but... I guess I've just been having a little trouble with, well, sitting still? I know that probably sounds kind of silly for an 18-year-old to say. But whenever I'm supposed to just stay put in the radiology suite for my training, or when I'm sitting in my college classes, I get this intense feeling like I'm... I don't know, almost crawling out of my skin? 

I've really been trying to just tough it out on my own for the last few months because I didn't want to be a bother to anyone, but no matter how hard I try to be good and stay seated, I still end up shifting around constantly, or pacing, or just finding some excuse to get up and move. Is... is that the kind of thing that's okay to come in for? I just want to make sure I'm not wasting your time.

symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient reports 'shifting around constantly' when trying to sit still.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient mentions 'finding some excuse to get up and move' when expected to stay seated in class or the radiology suite.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes an intense feeling of 'crawling out of my skin' and pacing when expected to sit still.

turns.doctor_question: Have you started taking any new medications, or changed the dose of any current medications, in the few months before this feeling started?
turns.patient_response:
Um, no, actually. I haven't started taking anything new at all. And I don't really take any regular medications right now, so there wasn't anything to change the dose of, either. 

I kind of wish it was just a medication side effect, because then it would be an easy fix for you to figure out, right? But no, it's just... just been happening on its own. I hope that's a helpful answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so I don't make your job harder.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel this need to move or pace even when you are completely alone and relaxed, or does it only happen when you are in situations where you feel you need to perform or be evaluated?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... wow, that's a really good question. I'm actually not entirely sure? I hope it's okay that I don't have a perfect answer for that. 

I guess I haven't really paid close enough attention to whether it happens when I'm totally alone and just hanging out, versus when I'm at the clinic or in class. I mean, I try really hard to just, you know, chill out when I'm by myself so I'm not driving my family crazy, but... I don't know if I still feel that exact same urge to pace then, or if I'm just not noticing it as much because no one is watching me? 

I'm really sorry, I know that's probably not very helpful. Is that a bad answer? I can definitely try to keep a better eye on it from now on and take notes if that would make things easier for you!

turns.doctor_question: When you are in class or at your training, do you find that your mind often wanders or that you have a hard time staying focused on the tasks at hand?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... no, I don't think so? I mean, I really try my absolute best to pay attention to my instructors and my professors. I definitely don't want you to think I'm just, like, daydreaming or slacking off, because I really do care about my training! 

I feel like my focus is actually pretty okay. It's really just the sitting still part that gets me. Like, I can listen to everything they're saying and follow along, I just... I just have to be bouncing my leg or shifting around in my chair while I do it. 

I hope it's okay to say no to that one? I just want to be completely honest with you so I'm not giving you the wrong impression about how I'm doing in school. Does that make sense?

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient notes that 'the sitting still part' is what gets them, indicating feelings of restlessness.
symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly denies having a hard time staying focused, stating their focus is 'pretty okay'.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of this need to move, do you find yourself feeling constantly worried or anxious about many different things in your daily life?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm constantly worried about a bunch of different things. I hope that's the right answer? 

I really try to keep a positive attitude, you know? I don't want to be someone who just complains or stresses out all the time. I mean, sure, I care about doing a good job at my clinicals and making sure my patients are okay, but I wouldn't call it, like, constant anxiety or anything. I just want to do my best. 

I'm really just struggling with the moving around part. I hope I'm not making this confusing by not having all these other symptoms. Is it okay that I'm just mostly dealing with the physical restlessness? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly states they are struggling with 'the moving around part' and 'physical restlessness'.
symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies feeling constantly worried or anxious about many different things.

turns.doctor_question: Looking back at your time in elementary or middle school, did you feel this same need to move around or fidget during class back then?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... yeah, actually. I hope it's okay to admit that, but... yeah, it's been going on for a really long time. 

My parents, um... they actually still talk about my elementary school parent-teacher conferences. Apparently, the teachers were always saying I was constantly out of my seat, or, you know, blurting things out, or rushing to start things before they even finished giving the directions. 

I guess I was a bit of a handful back then, which I feel really bad about! I definitely wasn't trying to be disruptive or anything, I just... I had a lot of energy, I guess? But yeah, it was definitely happening way before middle school, and definitely way before my radiology training started. 

Is that helpful to know? I hope I'm not making myself sound like a terrible student, I really do try my best to be good!

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient states that teachers reported they were 'constantly out of my seat' in elementary school.
